answer: Each epoch a public randomness beacon refracts one master task through a prism into many spectrally-distinct bands; your address fixes which band you must solve, and rewards vest only up a slow terrace: newcomers are capped at the lowest step and climb one level per many epochs of on-time, beacon-anchored solves. A sybil fleet on one host collides onto the same few bands, so its masks split a single bands payout while each still burns full compute and must independently wait out the terrace climb: N fakes earn sublinearly yet pay linearly in compute and real wall-clock time.
